glosses: when (I) did … , it turned out that
patterns.usage_note: Attached to the plain past form of a verb, this reports an actual one-off action and the outcome that happened to come to light because of it, so the following clause is almost always in the past tense and states a fact rather than a plan or a request. Unlike 〜たら it is never hypothetical, and unlike 〜と it does not describe a habitual or general consequence. It leans written and businesslike (reports, inquiries, apologies), which is why 調べたところ and 問い合わせたところ are its most typical hosts.

examples.ruby: 棚[たな]の裏側[うらがわ]を覗[のぞ]き込[こ]んだところ、鍵[かぎ]が落[お]ちていた。
examples.english: When I peered behind the shelf, there was the key on the floor.

examples.ruby: 駅[えき]の窓口[まどぐち]で聞[き]いてみたところ、次[つぎ]のバスは三十分[さんじゅっぷん]後[ご]だった。
examples.english: I asked at the station window, and it turned out the next bus wasn't for another thirty minutes.

examples.ruby: 体温[たいおん]を計[はか]ったところ、思[おも]ったより熱[ねつ]が高[たか]かった。
examples.english: I took my temperature, and it was higher than I'd thought.
